item.text:
I’d harden two areas.

`averageItemPrice` is currently brittle in two ways. In [test/orders.js](/abs/path/C:/Users/Kerim/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-eco-bench-J014pF/test/orders.js:18), it divides a quantity-weighted total by `items.length`, which is not actually an average item price unless every `qty` is `1`. It also returns `NaN` for an empty array. I’d either rename it to reflect “average line total” or change the implementation to divide by total quantity and explicitly handle `[]`.

I’d also add input validation around the public helpers. Right now [test/orders.js](/abs/path/C:/Users/Kerim/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-eco-bench-J014pF/test/orders.js:3), [test/orders.js](/abs/path/C:/Users/Kerim/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-eco-bench-J014pF/test/orders.js:11), and [test/orders.js](/abs/path/C:/Users/Kerim/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-eco-bench-J014pF/test/orders.js:23) assume well-formed data. Missing `items`, non-numeric `price`/`qty`, or a malformed `order` will throw or produce `NaN`. Even lightweight guards would make failures deterministic and easier to debug.
